subject: physics
title: Density, pressure and upthrust
key_idea: Density is mass per unit volume and pressure is force per unit area. Pressure in a fluid grows with depth as Δp = ρgΔh. An object in a fluid feels an upthrust equal to the weight of the fluid it displaces.

blocks.text: This section defines the two quantities and gives their equations.

items.meaning: Mass per unit volume of a substance.
The normal force acting per unit area.
A liquid or a gas. A fluid can flow.

blocks.label: Pressure
where: F = force at right angles to the surface, in N

items: The equation p = F/A applies to solids, liquids and gases.
For the same force, a smaller area gives a larger pressure.
Density = mass ÷ volume. Pressure = force ÷ area.
Use kg/m³ for density and Pa for pressure.

blocks.text: In a fluid at rest the pressure increases with depth. It depends on the depth, the density and g.

items.text: Imagine a column of fluid of cross-sectional area A and height Δh.
Its volume is AΔh, so its mass is m = ρAΔh.
Its weight is mg = ρAΔhg. This is the extra force on the area A at the bottom.
Δp = F / A = ρAΔhg / A = ρgΔh.

blocks.label: Hydrostatic pressure
where: Δp = change in pressure, in Pa
ρ = density of the fluid, in kg/m³
Δh = change in depth, in m

diagram.alt: A slider showing how the pressure due to the liquid increases with depth for different liquids.

items: At the same depth in the same fluid, the pressure is the same in every direction.
The total pressure at depth is the pressure due to the fluid plus the pressure at the surface, for example atmospheric pressure.
Δp = ρgΔh comes from the weight of a column of fluid.
Pressure rises in proportion to depth and to density.

blocks.text: A fluid pushes up on any object placed in it. This force is called upthrust.

items.meaning: The upward force a fluid exerts on an object that is partly or wholly in it.
The upthrust on an object equals the weight of the fluid it displaces.

blocks.label: Upthrust
where: ρ = density of the fluid, in kg/m³
V = volume of fluid displaced, in m³

items: The mass of fluid displaced is ρV, so its weight is ρVg.
V is the volume of the object that is **under the surface** of the fluid.
If the upthrust equals the weight of the object, it floats.
If the weight is greater than the upthrust, it sinks.
An object floats in a fluid when its average density is less than the fluid density.
Upthrust = weight of fluid displaced = ρgV.
A floating object has upthrust equal to its weight.

checks.q: A block has a mass of 0.54 kg and dimensions 0.10 m × 0.050 m × 0.040 m. Calculate its density.
Calculate the increase in pressure on a diver who goes 12 m deeper in sea water of density 1030 kg/m³.
A solid of volume 3.0 × 10⁻³ m³ is fully submerged in water of density 1000 kg/m³. Calculate the upthrust on it.

blocks.text: You must explain upthrust as the result of a pressure difference.

items.text: The pressure on the bottom of a submerged object is greater than on its top, because the bottom is deeper.
Force = pressure × area, so the upward force on the bottom is greater than the downward force on the top.
For a block of height Δh and area A: F = ρgΔh × A = ρgV.
The resultant upward force is the upthrust. It equals the weight of the fluid displaced.

items: The pressure in a fluid is written p = hρg, where h is the depth below the surface.
Explain upthrust on an object in a fluid and state Archimedes' principle.
